task.description:
Produce design artefact(s) for 4 MUST requirements from docs/requirements.yaml (stage 16): PAR-01 (events/events_archive PARTITION BY RANGE (created_at), monthly partitions events_YYYY_MM, PK widened to (event_id, created_at), separate plat_event_idempotency table for global idempotency-key uniqueness across partitions), PAR-02 (daily plat_partition_maintenance job keeping lead_months=2 future partitions attached, idempotent), PAR-03 (partition-scoped retention via DETACH/ATTACH CONCURRENTLY between events and events_archive, DROP TABLE confined to events_ephemeral partitions only), PAR-04 (CHECK constraints required on a standalone table before ATTACH PARTITION for fast catalog-only attach; AttachScanRequired error if missing). Read the full requirement bodies directly from docs/requirements.yaml (yaml.safe_load, utf-8-sig) -- read every acceptance criterion. THIS IS A HIGH-RISK BATCH touching the core events table (used throughout the entire platform, has existed since migration 001, has 20+ later migrations touching it).

CRITICAL SCOPING NOTE, confirmed by reading PAR-01 See: and PAR-05's body directly: PAR-05 ('the conversion' -- online conversion of an EXISTING populated events table into a partitioned parent via parallel-table-build + backfill + rename-swap) is EXPLICITLY A SEPARATE, LATER requirement, not in this batch. This batch (PAR-01-04) defines the TARGET partitioned schema and its steady-state behaviors (writes, maintenance, retention, attach-safety) -- it does NOT need to solve live-table conversion. Design this batch's migration(s) as creating events/events_archive ALREADY partitioned from the start (appropriate for how migrations apply to a fresh/freshly-migrated test database in this project's test infrastructure, which re-applies the full migration set from migration 001 onward on every fresh bpm_test provisioning) -- do NOT attempt an online conversion of already-existing data in this batch's migration; that mechanism is PAR-05's job. If the existing events table already has significant production-relevant history that would make a naive DROP+recreate genuinely unsafe for docs/anti-patterns.md reasons (irreversible data loss), flag this explicitly as an open question for REQ-ANALYST/ORCH rather than silently picking an unsafe migration approach -- but note the test database this batch validates against is freshly migrated, not a copy of production, so this tension may not actually block the design.

Read migrations/001_event_store.sql, 003_event_archive.sql, 013_event_archive_idempotency.sql, 027_adp01_event_store_tenant.sql, and any GBL- migrations touching events/events_archive schema shape, before designing -- you must understand the CURRENT full shape of both tables (all columns, indexes, constraints) since the new partitioned schema must preserve everything existing code depends on. Read src/event_store/*.zig to see what queries/assumptions existing code makes about the events table shape.

REWORK 1 (routed by ORCH after CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR Step 1b FAIL, 2 BLOCKER issues, both PAR-03-scoped):
- [BLOCKER 1] PAR-03 AC1 (RetentionClassForbidden guard rejecting delete retention_class for protected-family event types INSTANCE_*/TASK_*/GATEWAY_*/EXECUTION_*) has no design element -- falsely attributed to ADP-11, which predates the retention_class column this same migration creates. Add: the call site (likely Registry.registerType() or a new admin config-update path) checking event_type prefix before permitting retention_class='delete', a RetentionClassForbidden error taxonomy entry, and validation-rule/access-control spec for whatever surface sets retention_class (user input, Security checklist applies).
- [BLOCKER 2] PAR-03's 'No DELETE statement SHALL run against events or events_archive at any point' is genuinely ambiguous (absolute codebase-wide prohibition vs. narrower 'PAR-03's own mechanism never deletes'), and src/event_store/store.zig:947 Store.archive() issues DELETE statements against these tables that would violate the absolute reading. CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR confirmed archive() has ZERO call sites in src/ (dead code, only referenced from tests/integration/event_store_integration_test.zig) -- not wired into main.zig or any live request path. RESOLUTION DIRECTION (avoids needing a REQ-ANALYST business-interpretation detour by making the design correct under EITHER reading of the ambiguous text): include archive()'s retirement/removal in THIS batch's design scope. Since it is confirmed dead code with no production callers, removing it (or rewriting it to route through PAR-03's new DETACH/ATTACH mechanism instead of DELETE, if the retirement path is cheaper as a redirect than a full removal) closes the ambiguity definitively rather than leaving it open -- the codebase then satisfies PAR-03's AC under the strict reading too, with no compliance gap regardless of which reading is 'correct.' Update the design doc to specify this and remove the deferred-to-follow-up language. If removing/rewriting archive() turns out to be non-trivial (e.g. its test file exercises meaningful assertions beyond the archive() call itself that would need preserving), describe the specific scope of that work in the design so BACKEND-DEV isn't guessing, but do not leave the AC-compliance question itself open.
acceptance_criteria: Every acceptance criterion in PAR-01, PAR-02, PAR-03, PAR-04 is covered by the design
Design explicitly scopes out PAR-05's live-conversion mechanism and states why (fresh test DB vs. existing production data)
New partitioned schema design preserves every column/index/constraint the current events/events_archive tables have (verified against existing migrations, not assumed)
Existing src/event_store/*.zig code paths assessed for what changes the PK widening (event_id -> (event_id, created_at)) requires there

result.summary: REWORK 1 resolved both PAR-03-scoped BLOCKER issues from CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR Step 1b. ISSUE 1 (AC1 RetentionClassForbidden gap): added a full design element to par-03-partition-scoped-retention.md - call site is Registry.registerType() in src/event_store/registry.zig (the only write path to event_type_registry in src/; no admin HTTP route exists yet), via a new retention_class field on RegisterParams and a new check appended to the existing no-DB-access validateRegisterParams() pre-write validator, matching ISS-0148's established pattern. Added RegistryError.RetentionClassForbidden to the error taxonomy, plus a second, DB-level backstop CHECK constraint (chk_retention_class_protected_family, split_part(name, '_', 1) NOT IN (...)) added in the same migration/commit as the Zig-side guard (atomic-unit rule from docs/anti-patterns.md), since event_type_registry has no other write-path protection against direct SQL. Documented access control: retention_class is platform-admin configuration (no tenant_id column, shared across all tenants), so any future HTTP route exposing it MUST gate on actor.is_platform_admin (matching the existing pattern at src/api/routes/dlq.zig:238 and tasks.zig:854) - satisfies security-invariants.md INV-2 applied to the write boundary. Updated templates/specs/par-03-retention-class.migration.yaml with the second CHECK and a new test case; both tools/lint_design_artefact.py and tools/codegen_migration.py --dry-run pass clean. ISSUE 2 (Store.archive() vs PAR-03 DELETE-prohibition): read archive() (src/event_store/store.zig:947-1164) and all 5 of its calling integration tests in full. Confirmed independently (not just trusting the validator) zero src/ call sites - the similarly-named store.archive(allocator, id) sites in definitions.zig resolve to an unrelated definition.Store.archive() workflow-status function. Removal is NOT a clean, consequence-free deletion: archive() is the sole executable implementation of ES-07's (SHOULD, RELEASED) archival-move mechanics and drives 4 of tests/specs/ADP-11.md's traced test cases for ADP-11 (MUST, RELEASED) - TC-ES-07-01, TC-ES-07-02, TC-ADP-11-02, TC-ADP-11-03. TC-ADP-11-01 (ADP-11's own config-time-rejection AC) is unaffected, since it only calls upsertRetentionPolicy(), which this design does NOT remove. Resolution: full removal of archive() (not a rewrite-to-redirect - PAR-03's DETACH/ATTACH is whole-partition granularity, archive() is arbitrary-row granularity selected by per-event-type policy, so no mechanical redirect exists without silently changing ES-07's policy semantics), specified as same-batch, same-commit BACKEND-DEV scope: delete the function in full, keep upsertRetentionPolicy() and its ADP-11 guard, rewrite the 4 dependent tests to (a) assert the row-level mechanism is retired rather than SkipZigTest (forbidden by anti-patterns.md), and (b) repoint ES-07/ADP-11's archival-mechanics AC coverage at PAR-03's own PartitionRetention.runArchivalAging()/runEphemeralDrop() module (already designed, this same batch, being implemented later in this same workflow - not a deferred follow-up requirement). Added a mechanical closure proof: git grep for 'DELETE FROM events'/'DELETE FROM events_archive' in src/ must return zero results after removal, closing the AC-compliance question under EITHER reading of PAR-03's ambiguous DELETE-prohibition text simultaneously, with no REQ-ANALYST business-interpretation detour needed. Removed all 'defer to follow-up' language from both par-03-partition-scoped-retention.md (Open questions #1, now RESOLVED) and par-01-monthly-range-partitioning.md (Open questions #7 and the Existing-code-paths bullet, both now RESOLVED, pointing to PAR-03's design as the authoritative removal scope). All 3 modified artefacts pass tools/lint_design_artefact.py with 0 issues.
